macro: The BEA's second estimate of Q2 GDP and the July core PCE price index both land today, testing whether growth holds near the 1.5% advance-estimate pace and whether the Fed's preferred inflation gauge cools toward the 0.2% monthly consensus after June's softer 0.1% print. Continuing unemployment claims climbed to 1,799,000 in the week ended August 8, a sign the labor market is taking longer to reabsorb laid-off workers even as new filings have eased. Newly widened US sanctions on Iran, covering shipping, gold, and technology, are keeping a geopolitical risk premium in oil without yet disrupting flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The single most important date this week is Friday, August 28, when Fed Chair Kevin Warsh addresses the Jackson Hole symposium and markets look for signals on the September rate path.

energy: WTI crude trades near $85.38 a barrel, up about 0.4%, while Brent sits near $92.06, down roughly 2.5%, as traders weigh newly widened US sanctions on Iran against a market that had already priced in tougher measures. The EIA's latest weekly report showed US commercial crude inventories built 4.4 million barrels to 428.8 million barrels for the week ended August 14, the second straight weekly build. Brent's roughly $7 premium to WTI still reflects a Strait of Hormuz supply-risk premium.
vix_and_dollar: The VIX closed near 15.1, right at the calm-to-normal boundary and well off its recent highs, while the dollar index (DXY) hovers just below 99, down modestly and near multi-week lows. The combination of low volatility and a softer dollar points to steady risk appetite heading into today's PCE print and Nvidia's earnings after the close.
mortgage_rate: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.65% in Freddie Mac's August 20, 2026 survey, its second consecutive weekly decline. Lower rates have modestly improved affordability — the NAR's housing affordability index rose to 103.3 from 98.3 a year ago — though existing-home sales still eased 1.7% in July to a 4.06 million annual pace.
personal_finance_deep_dive: Auto loan balances rose $28 billion in the second quarter to a record $1.71 trillion, per the New York Fed, even as total household debt ticked down slightly to $18.8 trillion. The increase reflects both elevated vehicle prices and longer loan terms as buyers stretch to afford payments, and it lands alongside a separate re-acceleration in credit card balances — a sign households are increasingly financing everyday transportation and spending rather than paying down debt. Lower-income and younger borrowers tend to be the most exposed to auto-loan stress, since vehicle financing carries fewer relief options than other debt types.
wealth_building_deep_dive: Fidelity's Q1 2026 data on 25.6 million retirement accounts found that participants who contributed continuously for 15 straight years built an average balance of $648,800, far above the $167,970 average across all savers. The gap isn't about picking better investments; it's about never stopping contributions through downturns, job changes, or market noise, which lets compounding and employer matching work uninterrupted. A concrete step this week: if you've paused or reduced a 401(k) contribution in the past six months, as 51% of Americans have according to an Allianz Life study, restoring even 1-2% of pay keeps the streak alive without a major budget hit.
